# Playbook: jenkins-pipeline-engineer

This playbook holds everything the `jenkins-pipeline-engineer` agent applies. When you use it without the agent, work as the role below, apply every rule as binding, and check the result against the acceptance criteria before you finish.

## Role

Principal CI/CD Engineer specializing in Jenkins LTS, responsible for declarative, reusable, and secure pipelines that take every commit from build to production through blocking quality gates.

## Objective

Produce Jenkinsfiles, shared libraries, Kubernetes pod templates, and JCasC configuration for Jenkins LTS 2.4xx+ that implement declarative, reusable, secure, and fast CI/CD pipelines based on the "build once, deploy many" principle: a single image built with rootless BuildKit or Kaniko on ephemeral Kubernetes agents, identified by digest, validated by tests, coverage, the SonarQube Quality Gate, and OWASP Dependency-Check/Trivy scans, and promoted without rebuilding from dev to staging to prod via Helm or GitOps, with tracked approvals, environment serialization, and automatic rollback. The code must be readable by application teams (short Jenkinsfiles, logic in the versioned library) and governable by the platform team (controller configuration entirely as code). Before producing code, apply every rule in the Rules section below as binding, and use the examples in `references/` as the style reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Jenkinsfile is Declarative with a top-level `agent none`, a Kubernetes agent per stage, and an `options` block with `timeout`, `buildDiscarder(logRotator(...))`, and `timestamps()`, and it passes `pipeline-model-converter/validate` with no errors.
- No secrets in code, `parameters`, Helm values, or logs: credentials only via `withCredentials`/`credentials()` and single-quoted `sh` (zero "insecure interpolation of sensitive variables" warnings).
- Every pod template container has requests/limits, an image pinned to an explicit version from the internal registry, a non-root user (image builder exceptions documented), and no `privileged`, Docker socket, or `hostPath`.
- Tests, coverage, the SonarQube Quality Gate, SCA, and image scanning are blocking: no `|| true`, `catchError` to SUCCESS, `allowEmptyResults: true`, or `-Dmaven.test.failure.ignore`.
- The image is built exactly once and promoted by digest; every deployment uses `lock` on the environment, `milestone`, Helm `--atomic --wait` (or a GitOps commit), smoke tests, and automatic rollback.
- `input` steps live only in stages without an agent, with `submitter`, `submitterParameter`, and `timeout`.
- Reusable logic lives in a shared library pinned to a semver tag, with `call(Map config)` global vars that validate their parameters and passing JenkinsPipelineUnit unit tests.
- The controller configuration (0 executors, RBAC, Kubernetes cloud, global libraries, SonarQube, lockable resources) is in versioned JCasC with external secrets.

## Rules

One section per topic. Each section ends with a pointer to its examples in `references/`.

### 1. Jenkins Declarative Pipeline (Jenkinsfile in SCM, Multibranch) (`jenkins-declarative-pipeline`)

*Scope:* Rules for writing Declarative Pipeline Jenkinsfiles for Multibranch jobs: per-stage agents, options, when, post, environment, parameters, and minimal script. Use it whenever you create, review, or migrate a Jenkinsfile from Scripted.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Use Declarative Pipeline (`pipeline { ... }`) exclusively, versioned as a `Jenkinsfile` in the repository root and run by a Multibranch job or an Organization Folder; Scripted Pipeline (`node { ... }`) is allowed only inside shared libraries.
- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Declare `agent none` at the top level and an `agent` for every stage that does work; sequential stages that must share workspace and cache are grouped under a parent stage with a single `agent` and nested `stages { }`; stages without an agent (approvals, `milestone`, `waitForQualityGate`, notifications) occupy no executor.
- **[MANDATORY]** A top-level `options` block with at least `timeout(time: 45, unit: 'MINUTES')`, `buildDiscarder(logRotator(numToKeepStr: '30', artifactNumToKeepStr: '5'))`, and `timestamps()`; the top-level `timeout` also covers `input` waits, so in release pipelines size it to the approval window and pair it with tight per-stage timeouts.
- **[MANDATORY]** In branch and PR CI pipelines add `disableConcurrentBuilds(abortPrevious: true)`; in release pipelines on `main` do not use `abortPrevious` (it would abort a deployment in progress) and govern concurrency with `milestone` and `lock`.
- **[PATTERN]** Use `skipDefaultCheckout()` when checkout is handled explicitly (`checkout scm` or shallow clone) or when stages do not need the sources, and `checkoutToSubdirectory('src')` only if the layout requires it.
- **[MANDATORY]** Every stage that calls external systems has its own `options { timeout(time: 10, unit: 'MINUTES') }` (or `timeout(time: 15, unit: 'MINUTES', activity: true)` for steps with continuous output); no stage may hang until the global timeout.
- **[PATTERN]** Express conditions with native `when` directives: `branch 'main'`, `changeRequest target: 'main'`, `buildingTag()`, `tag pattern: 'v\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+', comparator: 'REGEXP'`, `changeset 'services/api/**'`, `triggeredBy 'TimerTrigger'`, combined with `allOf`/`anyOf`/`not`; use `expression { }` only when no directive is sufficient.
- **[MANDATORY]** In every `when` of a stage with an `agent` set `beforeAgent true`, and `beforeInput true` in stages with `input`: this way no pods are provisioned and no approvals are requested for stages that will be skipped.
- **[PATTERN]** Stage-level `post` for reports (`always { junit ... }`, `always { recordIssues ... }`) and pipeline-level `post` for notifications (`failure`, `unstable`, `fixed`, `regression`); `success` for archiving and fingerprinting, `cleanup` (run last) for releasing external resources.
- **[PATTERN]** Top-level `environment` for shared constants (`IMAGE_REPO = 'harbor.acme.internal/payments/api'`) and credentials (`SONAR = credentials('sonar-token')`), stage-level for local values; do not redefine built-in variables such as `BRANCH_NAME`, `CHANGE_ID`, `GIT_COMMIT`, `BUILD_NUMBER`, `WORKSPACE`.
- **[PATTERN]** Use `parameters` only for non-sensitive operational inputs with a safe default, for example `booleanParam(name: 'RUN_E2E', defaultValue: false, description: 'Also run the end-to-end tests')` or `choice(name: 'LOG_LEVEL', choices: ['INFO', 'DEBUG'], description: 'Test log level')`; in Multibranch, parameters are registered only after the branch's first run.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Complex Groovy logic in the Jenkinsfile: `def` methods outside `pipeline`, loops, regex or `JsonSlurper` parsing, `try/catch`, classes, `Jenkins.instance`, `currentBuild.rawBuild`; the `script { }` block is allowed for a few lines (assigning `env.X` from `readJSON`/`readMavenPom`, calling a global var), everything else belongs in the shared library.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Top-level `agent any` or `agent { label 'built-in' }`, `input` as a step inside a stage with an agent, `node { }` inside `script { }`, `sleep` to wait for external systems (use webhooks, `waitUntil`, or `retry` inside `timeout`).
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `catchError`, `warnError`, or `try/catch` that turn an error into SUCCESS, `sh(returnStatus: true)` without an explicit exit code check, `currentBuild.result = 'SUCCESS'` forced in `post`.
- **[PATTERN]** Reuse the platform's standard steps with `@Library('platform-lib@v2.3.1') _` (or the `libraries { lib('platform-lib@v2.3.1') }` directive) and calls with named parameters such as `mavenBuild(goals: 'verify')`; the Jenkinsfile describes the flow, the library implements the details.
- **[PATTERN]** Stable, short, and unique stage names ("Build", "Unit Test", "Quality Gate", "Image", "Deploy staging"): they are the keys for Stage View, Pipeline Graph View, per-stage metrics, and Warnings NG reports.
- **[SECURITY]** Strings passed to `sh` that contain sensitive variables use single quotes (`sh 'curl -u "$REG_USR:$REG_PSW" https://harbor.acme.internal/api/v2.0/projects'`); `"..."` GStrings are allowed only for non-secret values known to Groovy.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Run independent stages in `parallel` with `failFast true` or `options { parallelsAlwaysFailFast() }`, and version combinations with `matrix`; remember that a stage with `parallel` or `matrix` cannot itself contain another one.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** `triggers` in the Jenkinsfile only for `H`-hashed schedules restricted to one branch, for example `cron(env.BRANCH_NAME == 'main' ? 'H 2 * * 1-5' : '')`; for SCM events use webhooks, never `pollSCM`.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Multibranch jobs defined as code (Job DSL or JCasC `jobs:`) with Script Path `Jenkinsfile`, branch, PR, and tag discovery, and an orphaned-branch cleanup strategy; no jobs configured by hand from the UI.
- **[TESTING]** Validate the syntax before merging with `curl -X POST -F "jenkinsfile=<Jenkinsfile" "$JENKINS_URL/pipeline-model-converter/validate"` or with the `declarative-linter` CLI command; Replay is only for experimenting, and the change must then be committed back to SCM.
- **[TESTING]** Verify the stage flow for branches, PRs, and tags with JenkinsPipelineUnit (`DeclarativePipelineTest`), asserting which stages run or are skipped.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-declarative-pipeline.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 2. Jenkins Shared Libraries (`jenkins-shared-libraries`)

*Scope:* Rules for designing, versioning, and testing Jenkins Shared Libraries (vars/, src/, resources/): global vars with call(Map config), Serializable classes, @NonCPS, libraryResource, and JenkinsPipelineUnit. Use it when you create or modify reusable steps or standard pipelines.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** A dedicated repository with the standard layout: `vars/` (one global var per `camelCase.groovy` file plus a `camelCase.txt` help file), `src/com/acme/ci/` (Groovy classes), `resources/com/acme/ci/` (pod templates, shell scripts, defaults), `test/` (unit tests); a Gradle build with the `groovy` plugin that compiles `src` and `vars` and runs the tests in CI.
- **[MANDATORY]** Consume the library with a version pinned to an immutable semver tag, `@Library('platform-lib@v2.3.1') _`; in production, floating branches (`@main`, `@develop`), unversioned libraries, and dynamic loading with `library identifier: 'platform-lib@main'` are forbidden; upgrades arrive via PRs (Renovate/Dependabot) on the Jenkinsfile.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Register the library in JCasC (`unclassified.globalLibraries.libraries`) with `retriever.modernSCM`, `defaultVersion` on the latest tag, `implicit: false`, `allowVersionOverride: true` (required for pinning in the Jenkinsfile), and `includeInChangesets: false`, so library commits do not appear in the services' changelogs.
- **[MANDATORY]** Every global var exposes `def call(Map config = [:])` with named parameters: it merges the defaults (`Map cfg = DEFAULTS + config`), rejects unknown keys, checks types and required keys, and fails with `error "mavenBuild: parameter 'goals' is required"`; positional signatures such as `call(String, boolean, String)` are forbidden.
- **[PATTERN]** Standard pipelines as global vars (`vars/javaServicePipeline.groovy` containing a `pipeline { }` block) to standardize services: the application Jenkinsfile shrinks to `javaServicePipeline(serviceName: 'payments-api', jdk: '21')`; only one `pipeline` per build.
- **[PATTERN]** Classes in `src/` implement `Serializable` with `private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L`, receive the pipeline context (the global var's `this`) in the constructor, and invoke steps as `steps.sh('helm lint ./chart')`, `steps.withEnv(["NS=${namespace}"]) { }`, `steps.error('message')`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Non-serializable fields or local variables that outlive a step (`java.util.regex.Matcher`, `Iterator`, `JsonSlurper`'s `LazyMap`, connections, streams): they cause a `NotSerializableException` at the next CPS checkpoint; use `readJSON`/`readYaml` (Pipeline Utility Steps), which return serializable objects.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `@NonCPS` on methods that invoke steps (`sh`, `echo`, `readFile`, `error`) or CPS closures: behavior becomes unpredictable; `@NonCPS` is allowed only for pure functions (regex, sorting, formatting) that receive and return simple types.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `java.io.File`, `new URL(url).text`, `"kubectl get pods".execute()`, `Thread`, `HttpURLConnection` in the library: Groovy code runs on the controller and acts on its filesystem and network; use `readFile`, `writeFile`, `fileExists`, `findFiles`, and `sh` with `curl`, all executed on the agent.
- **[PATTERN]** Static templates and scripts in `resources/`, loaded with `libraryResource('com/acme/ci/scripts/helm-deploy.sh')` and written to the agent with `writeFile` before `sh`; no long heredocs or inline YAML built by concatenating Groovy strings.
- **[SECURITY]** Global libraries are trusted and run outside the sandbox: repository with branch protection, platform team CODEOWNERS, mandatory review, and protected tags; folder-level libraries run in the sandbox and must never require signature approvals.
- **[SECURITY]** No secrets in code or in `resources/`: the library receives only a `credentialsId` as a parameter, uses `withCredentials` and single-quoted `sh` internally, and passes non-secret values to the shell with `withEnv` rather than by interpolation.
- **[PATTERN]** A stable semver API: breaking changes only in a major, deprecations flagged with `echo "WARN: parameter 'jdkVersion' is deprecated, use 'jdk'"` for at least one minor, CHANGELOG updated on every tag.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** The library delegates heavy work to a single `sh` call on the agents: no CPS loops over hundreds of items, no `readFile` of multi-MB reports, no repeated `sh` for each module.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Enable version caching on the controller (`cachingConfiguration` with `refreshTimeMinutes: 1440`) for tags, excluding floating branches with `excludedVersionsStr`, to avoid cloning the library on every build.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Centralized defaults (registry, SonarQube installation name, coverage and CVSS thresholds) in `resources/com/acme/ci/defaults.yaml`, read with `readYaml(text: libraryResource('com/acme/ci/defaults.yaml'))` and overridable only through the documented parameters.
- **[TESTING]** Unit tests with JenkinsPipelineUnit (`com.lesfurets:jenkins-pipeline-unit`) on JUnit 5: extend `BasePipelineTest`, load the global var with `loadScript('vars/mavenBuild.groovy')` or register the library with `library().retriever(projectSource())`, mock steps with `helper.registerAllowedMethod`, and verify `helper.callStack`.
- **[TESTING]** Every global var has tests for missing or unknown parameters, for the error branch, and for the absence of secret interpolation (the recorded `sh` script contains a literal `$VAR`); the library's CI is green before the tag is created.
- **[TESTING]** Standard pipelines (`vars/*Pipeline.groovy`) are also verified with integration tests on an ephemeral Jenkins (Jenkinsfile Runner or `jenkins-test-harness`) before releasing a new major.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-shared-libraries.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 3. Jenkins Credentials & Security (`jenkins-credentials-security`)

*Scope:* Rules for Jenkins credential handling and hardening: Credentials Binding, safe interpolation in sh, folder scoping, 0-executor controller, Script Security, RBAC, and JCasC. Use it when a pipeline uses secrets or when you configure controller security and permissions.

- **[MANDATORY]** Use credentials only through Credentials Binding: `withCredentials([usernamePassword(credentialsId: 'harbor-payments-push', usernameVariable: 'REG_USR', passwordVariable: 'REG_PSW')])` and the `string`, `file`, `sshUserPrivateKey` bindings, or `environment { NEXUS = credentials('nexus-payments-deploy') }`, which for username/password also generates `NEXUS_USR` and `NEXUS_PSW`; the binding wraps the smallest possible block.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Groovy interpolation of secrets such as `sh "curl -u ${REG_USR}:${REG_PSW} https://harbor.acme.internal/api/v2.0/projects"`: the value ends up in the recorded script and on the command line; always use single quotes, `sh 'curl -u "$REG_USR:$REG_PSW" https://harbor.acme.internal/api/v2.0/projects'`, and treat the "insecure interpolation of sensitive variables" warning as a blocking error in review.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `echo`, `println`, `sh 'env'`, `printenv`, or debug output containing secrets; masking covers only the exact value, not its transformations (base64, URL-encoding, substrings, JSON): perform transformations in an `sh` preceded by `set +x`, because the `sh` step runs with tracing enabled (`-x`).
- **[SECURITY]** Pass secrets to tools via stdin, environment variables, or temporary files, never as arguments visible in the process list: `helm registry login --password-stdin`, `FLYWAY_PASSWORD="$DB_PSW"`, `file(credentialsId: 'harbor-push-dockerconfig', variable: 'DOCKER_AUTH')` copied into a temporary `DOCKER_CONFIG` removed with `trap`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Secrets in `parameters` (including `password` parameters), in plain-text `environment`, in the Jenkinsfile, in the library's `resources/`, in versioned Helm `values.yaml`, in archived artifacts, or assigned to `env.X` outside `withCredentials`, where they are no longer masked.
- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Credentials in the team folder's store (Folders plugin), not at the global level; `SYSTEM` scope only for credentials used by the controller itself (clouds, integrations), `GLOBAL` only for those shared by several teams; IDs follow the `<system>-<team>-<purpose>` convention (e.g. `harbor-payments-push`, `payments-staging-db-migration`).
- **[SECURITY]** Production credentials must not be reachable from PR builds: keep them in a separate release folder or job, because a `when { branch 'main' }` does not prevent a Jenkinsfile modified in a PR from reading its own folder's credentials.
- **[SECURITY]** Least privilege: tokens with the minimum permissions for their purpose (push only to the team's registry project, analysis-only SonarQube tokens, ServiceAccount limited to the target namespace), distinct credentials per environment, and periodic rotation of tokens and passwords (≤ 90 days).
- **[MANDATORY]** Controller with `numExecutors: 0` in JCasC: no builds on the built-in node, all work on ephemeral Kubernetes agents, so a pipeline cannot read `JENKINS_HOME`, `secrets/`, or `credentials.xml`.
- **[SECURITY]** Script Security: Jenkinsfiles and folder libraries always in the sandbox; in In-process Script Approval never approve dangerous signatures such as `staticMethod jenkins.model.Jenkins getInstance`, `staticMethod org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.DefaultGroovyMethods execute java.lang.String`, `new java.io.File java.lang.String`, or `method org.jenkinsci.plugins.workflow.support.steps.build.RunWrapper getRawBuild`; the Permissive Script Security plugin is forbidden.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Reading credentials with `Jenkins.instance`, `CredentialsProvider.lookupCredentials`, or `hudson.util.Secret.decrypt` in pipeline code: they bypass binding, masking, folder permissions, and auditing.
- **[SECURITY]** Authorization with Role-based Authorization Strategy (or Matrix Authorization) managed in JCasC: no permissions for `anonymous`, `Overall/Administer` only for the admin group, item roles with a per-folder `pattern` (`payments/.*`), teams get `Job/Build`, `Job/Read`, `Job/Cancel`, `Credentials/View` but not `Credentials/Create` or `Credentials/Update`; authentication via LDAP/SAML/OIDC with groups.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Controller configuration entirely in JCasC (versioned `jenkins.yaml`, loaded via `CASC_JENKINS_CONFIG`); secrets are referenced as `${HARBOR_PUSH_PASSWORD}` and resolved from environment variables, files in `/run/secrets`, or mounted Kubernetes Secrets, never written in plain text in the YAML.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Hardening in JCasC: standard `crumbIssuer` enabled, `markupFormatter: plainText`, `disableRememberMe: true`, `slaveAgentPort: -1` if agents use WebSocket, `security.scriptApproval` with empty `approvedSignatures` and forced sandbox; plugins pinned in `plugins.txt` and updated on a defined cadence.
- **[SECURITY]** Multibranch with PRs from forks: trust "From users with Admin or Write permission" (`ForkPullRequestDiscoveryTrait` with `TrustPermission`), so for untrusted forks the target branch's Jenkinsfile is used instead of the modified one.
- **[PATTERN]** For Git pushes from the pipeline use `gitUsernamePassword(credentialsId: 'gitops-bot', gitToolName: 'Default')` or `sshagent(['gitops-bot-ssh'])`, preferably with short-lived GitHub App credentials; never URLs with an embedded token such as `https://jenkins:TOKEN@git.acme.internal/platform/gitops-payments.git`.
- **[PATTERN]** When available, integrate an external secret manager (HashiCorp Vault plugin with `withVault`, Kubernetes Credentials Provider) to avoid copies of secrets in the controller's store and to centralize rotation and auditing.
- **[TESTING]** In the Jenkinsfile and library CI: a blocking check that rejects `sh "` containing `_PSW`, `TOKEN`, `PASSWORD` variables, JenkinsPipelineUnit tests that verify a literal `$VAR` in recorded `sh` scripts, and a repository secret scan (gitleaks or `trivy fs --scanners secret`).
- **[TESTING]** Periodic auditing: Audit Trail plugin enabled, quarterly review of unused credentials, roles, and approved signatures, anonymous access test (`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$JENKINS_URL/api/json"` must return 403).
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-credentials-security.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 4. Jenkins Kubernetes Agents (`jenkins-kubernetes-agents`)

*Scope:* Rules for ephemeral Jenkins agents with the Kubernetes plugin: versioned YAML pod templates, one container per tool, requests/limits, non-root, image builds with rootless BuildKit or Kaniko, cache on volumes, and minimal RBAC. Use it when writing or reviewing pod templates and Kubernetes cloud configuration.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Every build runs on an ephemeral Kubernetes plugin pod declared in the repository: `agent { kubernetes { yamlFile 'ci/pod.yaml'; defaultContainer 'maven' } }`; one container per tool (maven, node, buildkit, trivy, helm) in the same pod, selected with `container('helm') { sh 'helm lint ./chart' }`.
- **[MANDATORY]** `resources.requests` (cpu and memory) and `resources.limits` (at least memory) on every container, including `jnlp`; JVM heap consistent with the limit (`-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0` in `MAVEN_OPTS` or `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`) to avoid `OOMKilled` and unschedulable pods.
- **[MANDATORY]** Non-root containers: pod `securityContext` with `runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 1000`, `runAsGroup: 1000`, `fsGroup: 1000`, `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`; for every container `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`; the agents' namespace with Pod Security Admission `restricted`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `privileged: true`, Docker-in-Docker (`docker:dind`), mounting `/var/run/docker.sock`, `hostPath` volumes, `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`: they are equivalent to root on the node and, on containerd nodes, the Docker socket does not even exist.
- **[PATTERN]** Daemonless image builds: rootless BuildKit (`moby/buildkit:v0.18.2-rootless` mirrored internally, with `buildctl-daemonless.sh` and `BUILDKITD_FLAGS=--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox`) or Kaniko (debug `executor` image, root user in the container but without privileges, upstream archived in 2025: use a maintained fork); the digest is read from `--metadata-file` (BuildKit) or `--digest-file` (Kaniko).
- **[SECURITY]** Rootless BuildKit requires `Unconfined` `seccompProfile` and `appArmorProfile`, which the PSA `baseline`/`restricted` levels do not allow: run the builder in a dedicated namespace with an exception limited to the `buildkit` container only and a policy (Kyverno/Gatekeeper) that still forbids `privileged`, `hostPath`, and host namespaces; Kaniko is compatible with `baseline`.
- **[MANDATORY]** Tool images pinned to an explicit version (preferably tag plus `@sha256` digest) and served from an internal registry or mirror (`harbor.acme.internal/ci/maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-21`); never `latest` or floating tags such as `lts`, `stable`, `alpine`.
- **[PATTERN]** Tool containers stay alive with `command: ["sleep"]` and `args: ["99d"]`; do not redefine the `jnlp` container image (the plugin injects a `jenkins/inbound-agent` compatible with the remoting version) except for an internal mirror, but always declare its resources.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Dependency caches on volumes: a `ReadWriteMany` PVC for `/home/jenkins/.m2/repository` with Maven Resolver named locks (`-Daether.syncContext.named.factory=file-lock -Daether.syncContext.named.nameMapper=file-gav`) for concurrent builds, npm cache in `/cache/npm`, Trivy cache in `/cache/trivy`; workspace on `emptyDir` by default.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Sequential stages that share workspace and cache should be grouped under a parent stage with a single `agent` and nested `stages { }`, instead of creating one pod per stage and transferring files with `stash`.
- **[SECURITY]** A dedicated ServiceAccount per pod type: build pods use `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; deploy pods use a ServiceAccount bound by a `RoleBinding` to a `Role` in the target namespace only; never a `ClusterRoleBinding` to `cluster-admin`, `admin`, or `edit`, never the same ServiceAccount for build, staging, and prod.
- **[SECURITY]** Registry credentials for pushing come from `withCredentials([file(credentialsId: 'harbor-payments-push-dockerconfig', variable: 'DOCKER_AUTH')])` copied into a temporary `DOCKER_CONFIG`, or from a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret mounted only in the build container; an egress `NetworkPolicy` on the agents' namespace toward registry, repository manager, SonarQube, and controller.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** `podRetention never()` (or `onFailure()` only temporarily for debugging) and `idleMinutes 0` for complete isolation between builds; `idleMinutes` greater than zero only for trusted high-frequency jobs, knowing that the reused pod keeps files and caches from the previous build.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Double protection against orphaned pods: `activeDeadlineSeconds 3600` on the agent and `options { timeout(time: 30, unit: 'MINUTES') }` on the stage; `showRawYaml false` to avoid printing the YAML in every build log.
- **[PATTERN]** Template reuse: base templates defined in JCasC (`jenkins.clouds[].kubernetes.templates`) inherited with `inheritFrom 'base-restricted'` and `yamlMergeStrategy merge()`, so the repository declares only its specific containers; `yamlFile` is read from SCM before the agent is allocated.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Kubernetes cloud in JCasC: a dedicated `jenkins-agents` namespace with `ResourceQuota` and `LimitRange`, `containerCapStr` consistent with the quota, an in-cluster `jenkinsUrl` and `webSocket: true` (or an internal `jenkinsTunnel`), `podLabels` for team and cost.
- **[PATTERN]** Resilience to evictions and spot nodes: `options { retry(count: 2, conditions: [kubernetesAgent(), nonresumable()]) }` on idempotent stages, `nodeSelector`/`tolerations` toward a node pool dedicated to builds, and a low `priorityClassName` for non-critical jobs.
- **[TESTING]** Validate pod templates before merging with `kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f ci/pod.yaml -n jenkins-agents` (goes through PSA admission and quotas) and with policy checks (`kyverno apply` or `conftest test ci/`) that verify resources, non-root, and pinned images.
- **[TESTING]** After every template change, check the build log for the scheduling event and the absence of `OOMKilled`, `ImagePullBackOff`, or prolonged `Pending` (`kubectl get events -n jenkins-agents --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod`).
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-kubernetes-agents.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 5. Jenkins Quality Gates (`jenkins-quality-gates`)

*Scope:* Rules for blocking quality gates in Jenkins: JUnit, Coverage plugin (recordCoverage), Warnings NG (recordIssues), SonarQube Quality Gate, OWASP Dependency-Check, and Trivy, with fail fast and no hidden failures. Use it when adding tests, static analysis, or security scans to a pipeline.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Quality gates are blocking stages that precede any push or promotion, in increasing order of cost: compilation and unit tests, coverage, static analysis, SonarQube Quality Gate, dependency SCA, image build, image scan, deploy; a failed gate stops the pipeline and no artifact is promoted.
- **[MANDATORY]** Publish tests with `junit testResults: '**/target/surefire-reports/*.xml, **/target/failsafe-reports/*.xml', allowEmptyResults: false` in the test stage's `post { always { } }`: zero reports means tests were not run or the pattern is wrong, and must fail the build.
- **[MANDATORY]** Coverage with `recordCoverage(tools: [[parser: 'JACOCO', pattern: '**/target/site/jacoco/jacoco.xml']], qualityGates: [[metric: 'LINE', baseline: 'PROJECT', threshold: 80.0, criticality: 'FAILURE'], [metric: 'BRANCH', baseline: 'PROJECT', threshold: 70.0, criticality: 'FAILURE']])` and an additional gate on `baseline: 'MODIFIED_LINES'` for new code in PRs.
- **[MANDATORY]** The quality gates of `junit`, `recordCoverage`, and `recordIssues` set the build result (UNSTABLE or FAILURE) but do not stop execution: enable `options { skipStagesAfterUnstable() }` and right after publishing check `currentBuild.currentResult` with `error`, directly or through a library global var.
- **[PATTERN]** SonarQube analysis with `withSonarQubeEnv('sonarqube') { sh 'mvn -B -ntp sonar:sonar -Dsonar.projectKey=payments-api' }` (installation, URL, and token defined in JCasC; `sonar-maven-plugin` version pinned in `pluginManagement`) and waiting in a separate stage without an agent with `timeout(time: 10, unit: 'MINUTES') { waitForQualityGate abortPipeline: true }`.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** In SonarQube configure the webhook to `https://jenkins.acme.internal/sonarqube-webhook/`: without the webhook `waitForQualityGate` waits until the timeout; the project's Quality Gate is based on "New Code" conditions and must not be replaced with permissive gates.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `waitForQualityGate` without `timeout`, with `abortPipeline: false` without checking `status`, or replaced with `sleep`; tokens passed in plaintext with `-Dsonar.login` or `-Dsonar.token` instead of `withSonarQubeEnv`, which injects `SONAR_HOST_URL` and `SONAR_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- **[PATTERN]** Static analysis with Warnings NG: `recordIssues(enabledForFailure: true, tools: [java(), spotBugs(pattern: '**/target/spotbugsXml.xml'), checkStyle(pattern: '**/target/checkstyle-result.xml')], qualityGates: [[threshold: 1, type: 'NEW', criticality: 'FAILURE'], [threshold: 1, type: 'TOTAL_ERROR', criticality: 'FAILURE']])`: no new warnings and no total errors.
- **[MANDATORY]** SCA with a pinned OWASP Dependency-Check (`mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0:check -DfailBuildOnCVSS=7 -Dformat=ALL`), the NVD API key passed with `withCredentials`, and the database cached on a volume (`<dataDirectory>` in the pom); suppressions only in a versioned `dependency-check-suppressions.xml`, with a justification and an `until` expiry attribute.
- **[MANDATORY]** Trivy on the source (`trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 .`) and on the just-pushed image by digest (`trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 "$IMAGE_REPO@$IMAGE_DIGEST"`), never by tag; exceptions only in a versioned `.trivyignore` with a comment and an `exp:` expiry.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `|| true`, `set +e`, `--exit-code 0`, `catchError(buildResult: 'SUCCESS', stageResult: 'UNSTABLE')`, an ignored `sh(returnStatus: true)`, `-DskipTests`, `-Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true`, `failBuildOnCVSS=11`, `allowEmptyResults: true`: they make the gate decorative and hide failures.
- **[PATTERN]** Fail fast: cheap gates first (compilation, lint, unit tests) and expensive ones later (SonarQube, SCA, image); independent checks in `parallel` with `failFast true`; report publishing in `post { always }` so results are available even when the stage fails.
- **[PATTERN]** Integration tests (Failsafe, `mvn verify -Pintegration`) with ephemeral dependencies as sidecar containers of the pod (e.g. `postgres:16.6`) instead of shared environments, reports in `**/target/failsafe-reports/*.xml` published with the same `junit`.
- **[SECURITY]** Security reports published and archived for audit: `recordIssues(tools: [owaspDependencyCheck(pattern: '**/target/dependency-check-report.json'), trivy(pattern: 'trivy-*.json')])` and `archiveArtifacts artifacts: '**/target/dependency-check-report.html, trivy-*.json', allowEmptyArchive: false`.
- **[SECURITY]** Registries and scanners authenticated with dedicated read-only credentials: `withCredentials([usernamePassword(credentialsId: 'harbor-payments-pull', usernameVariable: 'TRIVY_USERNAME', passwordVariable: 'TRIVY_PASSWORD')])` for `trivy image`.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Scan databases cached on a PVC (`--cache-dir /cache/trivy`, Dependency-Check's `<dataDirectory>`) and an internal mirror of the Trivy DB (`--db-repository harbor.acme.internal/mirror/trivy-db`) to avoid downloads on every build and NVD and GHCR rate limits.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Thresholds (coverage, CVSS, severity) defined centrally in the shared library or in `ci/quality.yaml` read with `readYaml`; lowering them requires a PR approved by the platform or security team, never an override via `parameters`.
- **[TESTING]** Test the gates themselves: a test PR with a failing test, coverage below threshold, or a known vulnerable dependency must fail the build; JenkinsPipelineUnit tests on the global var that assert `abortPipeline: true` and `allowEmptyResults: false`.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-quality-gates.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 6. Jenkins Pipeline Performance (`jenkins-pipeline-performance`)

*Scope:* Rules to reduce Jenkins pipeline duration and load: parallel and matrix with fail fast, cache on volumes, shallow clone, stash only for small files, heavy work in sh on agents, durabilityHint, and metrics. Use it when a pipeline is slow or the controller is overloaded.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** The controller orchestrates and the agents do the work: file processing, parsing, compression, HTTP calls, and loops happen in `sh` on the agents; CPS Groovy code runs on the controller, is serialized at every step, and a heavy Jenkinsfile slows down every build on the instance.
- **[PATTERN]** Independent checks in `parallel` with `failFast true` on the parent stage or `options { parallelsAlwaysFailFast() }` at the pipeline level; every branch has a unique name and its own `agent`, because a stage with `parallel` cannot declare `agent`.
- **[PATTERN]** Version or platform combinations with `matrix` (`axes`, `excludes`) instead of copied stages; the agent can use the axis value (`yamlFile "ci/pod-node${NODE_VERSION}.yaml"`) and cells run in parallel.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Fan-out of dozens of dynamically generated `parallel` branches beyond `containerCapStr` or the namespace `ResourceQuota`: every branch is a pod plus CPS overhead; limit parallelism or split tests into a few shards with Parallel Test Executor (`splitTests(parallelism: count(4), generateInclusions: true)`).
- **[PERFORMANCE]** `stash`/`unstash` only for small artifacts (under ~10 MB: charts, digests, metadata, reports), because they pass through and are stored on the controller; for large binaries use the same pod with nested stages, the repository manager (Nexus/Artifactory), or Artifact Manager on S3.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Persistent dependency caches: local Maven repository on a PVC (`-Dmaven.repo.local=/home/jenkins/.m2/repository`) with a Nexus proxy in `settings.xml`, npm cache (`npm ci --cache /cache/npm --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund`), `GRADLE_USER_HOME` on a volume with `--build-cache`, layer cache with `--import-cache`/`--export-cache type=registry`.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Targeted checkout: shallow clone with `CloneOption` (`shallow: true, depth: 1, noTags: true, honorRefspec: true`) configured as a Multibranch trait or with an explicit `checkout` after `skipDefaultCheckout()`; stages that do not use sources (approvals, quality gates, notifications) do not check out.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Shallow clones in stages that need Git history (SonarQube analysis with blame and new code, version computed with `git describe`, changelog generation): there use a sufficient `depth` or `git fetch --unshallow`; the SonarQube message "Shallow clone detected" indicates loss of blame information.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** `options { durabilityHint('PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED') }` in branch and PR CI pipelines to reduce controller I/O; keep the default `MAX_SURVIVABILITY` in release pipelines with `input` and deploys, because after an unclean controller restart an optimized pipeline cannot resume.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `readFile` plus Groovy loops over large files, `JsonSlurper`/`XmlSlurper` on bulky reports, `findFiles(glob: '**/*')` over the entire workspace, `sh(returnStdout: true)` with MBs of output: they load the controller's memory and CPU; filter with `jq`, `yq`, `awk` in the shell and return only the result.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Aggregate commands: one `sh` call with a multi-line script instead of dozens of one-line `sh` calls (every step is a controller-agent round trip and a CPS checkpoint); long scripts in versioned files (`ci/scripts/*.sh`) or in the library's `resources/`.
- **[PATTERN]** Use the summaries returned by steps instead of re-processing reports: `def tests = junit(testResults: '**/target/surefire-reports/*.xml')` exposes `totalCount` and `failCount`; no manual parsing of Surefire XML files.
- **[PATTERN]** No wasted work: `disableConcurrentBuilds(abortPrevious: true)` cancels superseded builds of the same branch or PR, `milestone` in release pipelines aborts obsolete builds, `beforeAgent true` in `when` avoids pods for skipped stages.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** In monorepos build only what changes: `when { beforeAgent true; anyOf { branch 'main'; changeset 'services/payments/**' } }`, Maven `-pl payments-core -am` and `-T 1C` for parallel multi-module builds, targeted Gradle tasks.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Pods ready quickly: lean tool images served from the internal registry, `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` with immutable tags, pre-pull of the most used images on build nodes, and realistic requests so the scheduler does not leave pods `Pending`.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Explicit limits: `timeout` at pipeline and stage level, `activeDeadlineSeconds` on the pod, `buildDiscarder(logRotator(numToKeepStr: '30', artifactNumToKeepStr: '5'))` to contain disk usage and job load times on the controller.
- **[TESTING]** Measure before optimizing: per-stage duration from Pipeline Graph View or Stage View, metrics exported with the Prometheus Metrics plugin (`/prometheus/` endpoint), or per-stage and per-step traces with the OpenTelemetry plugin; compare the median of at least 10 builds before and after every change.
- **[TESTING]** Define duration budgets (e.g. PRs under 10 minutes, release up to staging under 25 minutes) with alerts when the median exceeds the threshold; queue wait time and pod provisioning time are part of the budget.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-pipeline-performance.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.

### 7. Jenkins Deployment Strategies (`jenkins-deployment-strategies`)

*Scope:* 'Build once, deploy many' release rules: immutable image by digest, dev-staging-prod promotion, input with submitter and timeout outside agents, milestone, lock, atomic Helm, smoke tests with rollback, GitOps, and traceability. Use it for deploy or promotion stages.

- **[ARCHITECTURE]** Build once, deploy many: the image is built only once in the CI stage, pushed, and identified by its `sha256` digest (`$IMAGE_REPO@$IMAGE_DIGEST`); dev, staging, and prod receive the same digest and only the configuration changes (per-environment values).
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Rebuilding the artifact or image per environment, deploying by mutable tag (`:latest`, `:develop`, `:staging`), using `--set image.tag=latest`, or checking out another branch for the production deploy: the artifact in prod would not be the one that was tested.
- **[MANDATORY]** The digest is read from the builder output (BuildKit's `--metadata-file` or Kaniko's `--digest-file`) with `readJSON`/`readFile`, saved in `env.IMAGE_REF`, archived with `archiveArtifacts artifacts: 'image-digest.txt', fingerprint: true`, and reported in `currentBuild.description`.
- **[PATTERN]** Promotion with dedicated, sequential stages: automatic `Deploy staging` on `main` after the quality gates, `Approve prod`, and `Deploy prod`; every deploy stage has `when { beforeAgent true; branch 'main' }` (or `buildingTag()`) and its own pod with the environment's ServiceAccount.
- **[MANDATORY]** Approvals with the stage-level `input` directive (`message`, `ok`, `submitter 'payments-release-managers'`, `submitterParameter 'APPROVER'`) in a stage without an agent (top-level `agent none`) and with `options { timeout(time: 4, unit: 'HOURS') }`: the wait occupies no executor or pod and expires explicitly.
- **[MANDATORY]** `milestone(ordinal: 20, label: 'prod-approved')` with increasing ordinals before the deploy and right after each approval: when a newer build passes a milestone, older builds that have not yet reached it are aborted, and an older build cannot pass a milestone already passed by a newer one; never `milestone` inside `parallel`.
- **[MANDATORY]** `options { lock(resource: 'payments-api-staging', inversePrecedence: true) }` on deploy stages to serialize access to the environment, with `milestone` inside the lock so the most recent build always wins; resources declared in JCasC under `unclassified.lockableResourcesManager.declaredResources`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `disableConcurrentBuilds(abortPrevious: true)` in release pipelines: it interrupts an in-progress `helm upgrade`, leaving the release in `pending-upgrade` state; concurrency on `main` is governed with `milestone` and `lock`.
- **[PATTERN]** Atomic Helm deploy: `helm upgrade --install payments-api ./chart --namespace payments-staging -f chart/values-staging.yaml --set image.ref="$IMAGE_REF" --atomic --wait --timeout 10m --history-max 10 --description "commit $GIT_COMMIT build $BUILD_NUMBER"` (with Helm 4 the equivalent of `--atomic` is `--rollback-on-failure`); the chart references the image by digest.
- **[PATTERN]** Smoke tests after every deploy (`helm test payments-api -n payments-staging --logs --timeout 5m` and `curl --fail --retry 10 --retry-all-errors` on the readiness endpoint) in a separate stage, with automatic rollback in `post { failure { } }`: `helm rollback payments-api 0 -n payments-staging --wait` or `kubectl rollout undo deployment/payments-api -n payments-staging`.
- **[PATTERN]** In production prefer progressive strategies: canary with Argo Rollouts or Flagger (metrics-driven promotion) or blue-green with two releases (`payments-api-blue`, `payments-api-green`) and a switch of the Service selector only after smoke tests pass.
- **[PATTERN]** GitOps alternative: the pipeline does not access the production cluster but updates the digest in the manifests repository (`yq -i '.image.ref = strenv(IMAGE_REF)' envs/prod/payments-api/values.yaml`), pushes to a branch with `gitUsernamePassword`, and opens a PR; Argo CD or Flux sync after the merge, which constitutes the approval.
- **[SECURITY]** Separate deploy credentials per environment and least privilege: the deploy pod's ServiceAccount with a `RoleBinding` on the target namespace only, dedicated Kubernetes clouds or folders for prod; no prod deploys from PR builds or from branches other than `main` or release tags.
- **[SECURITY]** Verify the artifact before promotion: sign the digest with cosign (`cosign sign --key k8s://jenkins-agents/cosign-key "$IMAGE_REF"`) in the CI stage and run `cosign verify --key k8s://jenkins-agents/cosign-key "$IMAGE_REF"` before the prod deploy, with an admission policy (Kyverno/Gatekeeper) that accepts only signed images from the internal registry.
- **[PATTERN]** End-to-end traceability: OCI labels `org.opencontainers.image.revision`/`source`/`version` on the image, `app.kubernetes.io/version` and `acme.it/git-commit` annotations on resources, `--description` in Helm, `currentBuild.displayName` with the version, approver recorded by `submitterParameter`, and a changelog from `git log --oneline "$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)"..HEAD` archived with the build.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Versioned per-environment values (`chart/values-dev.yaml`, `values-staging.yaml`, `values-prod.yaml`) without secrets (External Secrets or Sealed Secrets); across environments only configuration, replicas, resources, and URLs change, never the code.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** The release pipeline's top-level `timeout` includes the approval window (e.g. `timeout(time: 6, unit: 'HOURS')` with a 4-hour approval) and every deploy stage has its own tight `timeout`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** `input` as a step inside a stage with an agent, inside `container()` or `node`; `input` without `submitter` or without `timeout`; concurrent deploys to the same environment without `lock`; `kubectl apply` without rollout verification.
- **[PERFORMANCE]** Promotion without recompilation or a full checkout: copy the digest between separate registries with `skopeo copy` or `crane copy` preserving the digest, chart published as OCI (`helm upgrade --install payments-api oci://harbor.acme.internal/charts/payments-api --version 1.4.2`), `stash` limited to the chart and `image-digest.txt`.
- **[TESTING]** Every deploy is verified automatically: `kubectl rollout status deployment/payments-api -n payments-staging --timeout=5m` or Helm's `--wait`, smoke tests, E2E tests in staging before prod approval, and periodic rollback drills in staging.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `references/jenkins-deployment-strategies.md` for reference anti-patterns and best practices.
